# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual but cannot speak, and I only reach Deaf via gestures. Blind can only receive information by touch/reach, not by seeing gestures or hearing speech from me directly — so I cannot inform Blind directly at all. I must relay through Deaf, who can see my gestures, and Deaf can presumably speak to Blind (or gesture won't help Blind since Blind can't see).

So the chain must be: Mute --gesture--> Deaf --speak--> Blind.

I need to encode: cut yellow wire, press key marked 2, cut orange wire, press key marked 7, in that exact order.

I only have generic gesture symbols, no names. I need to build a convention with Deaf using gestures that map to concepts, but Deaf doesn't know my convention yet either. I should wait to see if Deaf sends anything first — but turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, so I go first with nothing yet learned. I'll send an initial gesture message trying to establish a numbered/ordered scheme, using distinct symbols for concepts: I'll pick ☝ for "step one", ✌ for "step two" etc., paired with symbols I associate with wire (🫲 maybe for "cut") and key (👆 for "press"). But Deaf needs to match symbol to color/number they see on the bomb, which I can't know is mapped correctly without feedback.

Best first move: signal step count and structure, then wait for Deaf's description next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🫲", "✌", "👆", "✌", "🫲", "🤟", "👆"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a keypad with four keys showing digits 2, 3, 7, 1 in that slot order, a strip with three engraved marks I cannot identify by sight, and six wires. The keypad wants 2 digits entered. Nothing entered yet. I need to know what the manual says before I press or cut anything.
Deaf says: Deaf reporting bomb state: Display shows 6. Light is green. Strip has three stripes painted red, blue, yellow in that order. Keypad has four buttons labeled 1 through 4 showing numbers 2, 3, 7, 1, it requires 2 digits entered, currently nothing entered. Wires numbered 1 through 6 are colored orange, yellow, blue, red, white, green respectively.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Excellent — now I have a full picture. Blind can hear Deaf speak (since Blind's message references needing manual info from me, but actually Blind said "to Mute" — wait, can Blind speak to me and can I hear? I cannot hear at all. But the transcript shows Blind's speech to me as text - that must be a system relay, not actual game channel... Actually the rules say Mute cannot speak, but can Mute hear? Nothing says Mute is deaf-in-ears. Mute "cannot speak" only. So Mute CAN hear! Good, that explains why I received Blind's spoken words and Deaf's spoken report.

So the channels are: Mute can hear (Blind and Deaf's speech) and can gesture to Deaf. Blind can hear (Deaf's speech) but not see gestures. Deaf can see gestures and speak, but not hear.

So the working path: I (Mute) hear everyone. I need to get the manual to Blind. Blind hears speech. But I cannot speak! Only Deaf can speak, and Deaf can hear nothing (so Deaf doesn't know the manual either, but I can gesture the manual steps to Deaf, who then speaks them to Blind).

Now mapping the manual to bomb specifics using Deaf's report:
- Yellow wire = wire numbered 2 (position 2)
- Orange wire = wire numbered 1 (position 1)
- Key wearing 2 = the key showing digit 2 (first keypad slot)
- Key wearing 7 = the key showing digit 7 (third keypad slot)

Order: cut yellow(wire#2), press key"2", cut orange(wire#1), press key"7".

I need to gesture this to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to Blind. I'll use gestures to represent: wire number 2, then key digit 2, then wire number 1, then key digit 7. I can use finger-count-like symbols: ✌ = two, ☝=one, and I need symbols for "wire" vs "key" action distinct from digits. Let me define: 🫲 = wire (cut), 👆 = key (press). Then digits via ☝✌✋... I'll use counting gestures matching finger counts for numbers 1,2,7. For 7 I can combine ✋(5)+✌(2) as concatenation meaning 5+2=7, or use 🤟 as a distinct token for "7" that I define now and reuse consistently.

Let me gesture clearly, step by step, marking each unit.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫲", "✌", "👆", "✌", "🫲", "☝", "👆", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 6, light is green. Strip stripes are red, blue, yellow in order - that matches my three engraved marks felt as first, second, third. Keypad buttons 1 through 4 show numbers 2, 3, 7, 1 - confirmed by touch too. Wires 1 through 6 are colored orange, yellow, blue, red, white, green. Please tell me what the manual says to do: which wire to cut by position number, or what 2 digit code to press by slot number.
Deaf says: Update: Display changed from 6 to 2. Light changed from green to blue. Strip, keypad, and wires are unchanged: strip red blue yellow, keypad values 2 3 7 1 needing 2 digits none entered yet, wires orange yellow blue red white green in slots 1 to 6. Display and light may be cycling or unstable, everything else looks fixed - suggest we anchor on the static elements.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf isn't speaking my gesture info to Blind yet — Deaf only sent me a "[☝]" acknowledgment gesture back, but hasn't relayed the manual steps to Blind via speech. I need to make sure Deaf understands my gestures precisely enough to speak them out as concrete instructions to Blind. Since gestures are ambiguous without a shared code, let me instead reconsider: maybe Deaf received my gestures but didn't know what to do with them (no established meaning). I should make my message unambiguous by leveraging the fact that Deaf already reported wire colors and keypad digits — I just need to tell Deaf plainly, via gesture-encoded numbers, the sequence of actions referencing positions Deaf already knows.

Given wire slots: 1=orange, 2=yellow, 3=blue, 4=red, 5=white, 6=green.
Keypad slots 1-4 show digits 2,3,7,1.

Manual: cut yellow (slot 2), press key showing 2 (slot 1), cut orange (slot 1), press key showing 7 (slot 3).

I'll gesture a clear sequence: action-type then slot-number, using consistent counting gestures (☝=1, ✌=2, ✋=5 as needed, or simple counts up to 6 using repeated finger symbols). Let me define: 🫲=cut-wire action, 👆=press-key action, and then use ☝✌🤟✊🖐🤚 as digits 1-6 respectively (single distinct symbols to avoid ambiguity from repetition). I'll pick:
1=☝, 2=✌, 3=🤟, 4=✊, 5=🖐, 6=🤚

Sequence: cut wire slot2 → 🫲 ✌
press key slot1 → 👆 ☝
cut wire slot1 → 🫲 ☝
press key slot3 → 👆 🤟

This tells Deaf: "cut wire#2, press key#1, cut wire#1, press key#3" — Deaf can translate slot numbers to actual colors/digits since Deaf already knows the mapping, and speak it to Blind in Blind's terms (position-based, which Blind confirmed matches).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫲", "✌", "👆", "☝", "🫲", "☝", "👆", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 4

then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: display now shows 2, light now shows blue instead of 6 and green. Everything else unchanged. If the manual has conditional instructions based on display number or light color, this may matter. Still waiting for your instructions on what action to take.

Mute, I am seeing your gestures but do not have a confirmed code key. If you are trying to send numbers, try one gesture per digit using the position in a simple 1 to 9 count with fingers style, for example one gesture equals digit 1, two equals digit 2, so I can decode reliably.

Let me use a clean finger-count style where the gesture itself visually represents the count: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5 is ambiguous for 4 — let me just use a strict list where I state which symbol equals which digit explicitly, then use it.

That's much safer and requires no prior shared vocabulary.

So to send digit N, I gesture the same symbol N times, separated somehow. But I need to distinguish groups (each number) — I can use a distinct "separator" gesture between numbers, e.g. 👋 as separator, and ☝ repeated as the tally.

Also need an action-type indicator: cut vs press. I'll use two different tally symbols: ☝ tally for "wire slot number", ✌ tally for "key slot number". Wait, better: use one tally symbol per count (✊ repeated) for the number itself, and prefix with a distinct single symbol to indicate action type: 🫲 = cut wire (before tally), 👆 = press key (before tally).

🫲 ✊ ✊ (cut, count=2) 👋(separator)
